name: Official TypeSafe skill
description: Official skill for writing Jev requests and choosing between Noul, Choice, and Score.

name: TypeSafe Python SDK
description: Official Python client, with a support-ticket routing example.

name: TypeSafe JavaScript SDK
description: Official JavaScript and TypeScript client.

name: Jevify
description: Agent skill for finding places to use Jev and planning comparisons with existing code.
notes: Independent skill, not the model or an official SDK.

name: Jev Logs
description: Scores log entries with Jev to decide which need a closer look.

name: Skillbox
description: Self-hosted skill library with optional Jev-based recommendations.
notes: Jev is an optional recommender, not required for the core library.

name: Jev Ultrafast
description: Jev picks browser actions and page elements; a separate model writes text.
notes: Published timing is a narrow author-run demonstration, not a general reliability guarantee.

name: Foreman
description: Uses Jev to check a coding agent's progress and decide when it needs intervention.
notes: Architectural experiment; its README provides an offline deterministic demo.

name: Jev MCP
description: MCP tools for checking claims against evidence, screening content, and ranking candidates.
notes: Review tool permissions and environment handling before installation.

name: TypeSafe MCP
description: Go MCP server for making Jev requests from coding agents.

name: Home Assistant Jev
description: Adds Jev decisions to Home Assistant entities and automations.
notes: Inspect the example automations and keep consequential actions behind explicit policy.

name: Jev Plays Snake
description: Snake where code finds legal moves and Jev picks a direction.
notes: Useful separation of legal-action generation, model choice, deadlines, and local execution.

name: JevPilot
description: Driving simulation where Jev chooses steering and speed. Not a real-world driving system.
notes: Simulation only; not an autonomous-driving safety system. The hosted demo may require login.

name: TypeSafe Mario
description: Jev picks controller inputs from emulator state. Requires a lawful local game setup.
notes: Requires a lawful local game setup; repository does not include Nintendo ROMs.

name: PROMPT FPS / Jev Doom
description: Jev chooses actions in a browser-based Doom engine. Uses Freedoom assets.
notes: Ships Freedoom, not commercial Doom assets. Engine and content have separate GPL/BSD notices; inspect licenses/.

name: Jev Music Playground
description: Jev picks musical parameters; code turns them into notes and MIDI. Includes an offline mode.
notes: Includes an explicitly labeled offline heuristic mode; Jev does not directly generate audio.

name: OpenJev SGLang
description: Independent typed-decision server using open models and SGLang. Not official Jev weights.
notes: Not official Jev weights; no requests go to TypeSafe. Review deployment authentication and GPU costs.

name: JevAI for XMage
description: Magic: The Gathering bots that use Jev alone or alongside XMage search.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21; a plugin inside an XMage fork. The reported 11-6-3 result is the hybrid across 20 author-run games with turn-cap draws, not our reproduction. Hybrid pruning is off by default. Review server-side keys, game assets, and licenses separately.

name: Jev Chess
description: A shared chess game against Jev with move probabilities. Hosted demo; source code not verified.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Public project-page metadata inspected, not server code. No public source repository or code license verified. No shared game move was submitted, and advertised results were not reproduced.

name: tisco
description: Searches video transcripts with Jev, then previews clip moves and renames for approval.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Transcript-based, not visual video understanding. Approved transcription uploads extracted audio; requests and transcript context reach OpenRouter. Documents a synthetic offline demo, paid live calls, and preview/undo controls. No clips or credentials were supplied for this review.

name: Vibe Domain
description: Ranks domain names by the requested style. Has a no-key heuristic mode and a hosted Jev option.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Public page reviewed; no public source repository or code license verified. Documentation distinguishes a no-key heuristic mode from live OpenRouter inference. No availability check or API call was run here. Recheck names at a registrar and review key handling before entering credentials.

name: jev_search
description: Ranks files by keyword, then checks their passages with Jev in two passes. Author marks it experimental.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Current README attributes file prioritization to keyword-density code, not Jev. The author marks the project fully AI-generated and not for production. Source text is sent through OpenRouter; inspect privacy and spending limits and prefer environment-based credentials. No code was executed.

name: Cua Driver + jev-use
description: Cua Driver example in Python and TypeScript: Jev chooses an action, the driver runs it, and code checks the result.
notes: Cua-maintained public-preview Python/TypeScript recipe, not a Jev model built into Driver. The mock path uses no Jev credentials but still operates a browser fixture. Live choices use hosted TypeSafe; screenshots are not sent to Jev by this adapter. Driver permissions, capture freshness, and independent postconditions remain application responsibilities.

name: Jev Cua (Codex/Waku)
description: Mac automation using Cua Driver, with optional Jev recommendations for saved workflows.
notes: Local runtime is not local Jev inference: the optional router sends best-effort-redacted requests and workflow descriptions to TypeSafe. Current README pins a specific Cua Driver version; review it before installing. Visual observations can disclose window contents to the connected client/model. Source-reviewed, not executed or security-audited.

name: jev-bot (@compootor)
description: Native Mac controls through a JavaScript MCP session, with optional Jev element selection.
notes: The @compootor/jev-bot package is distinct from unrelated repositories named jev-bot. Cua Driver is installed separately and requires desktop permissions. Direct element actions need no TypeSafe key; Jev actions do. The inspected version documents no browser-tab, coordinate-click, drag, scroll, clipboard, launch, or hotkey support. Persistent JavaScript is not a security sandbox.

name: Browser Harness (supporting driver)
description: The CDP browser connection used by Jev Ultrafast. Model-neutral, not a Jev model.
notes: Supporting infrastructure, not a Jev model or a claim that every Browser Harness task uses Jev. The dependency is declared in browser-use/jev-ultrafast/pyproject.toml. Remote debugging can expose a logged-in browser; use an isolated profile and review recording and permission settings.

name: TypeSafe computer use (macOS)
description: Mac automation using local OCR and accessibility data, with Jev choosing the next action.
notes: Requires macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions. Selected screen text enters model requests. Dry-run and explicit --act behavior are documented. Author cost/speed measurements were not reproduced. Previously indexed and featured in the X gallery; now also an editorial catalog selection.

name: Jev voice browser
description: Voice-controlled Playwright browser. Jev chooses actions from partial speech and page controls.
notes: A headed Chromium/Playwright application, not a native desktop driver. Uses a persistent browser profile and a loopback control server. Keep the control port private; speech processing and model requests can disclose content. Published timings are author-reported.

name: Jev Browser Skill
description: Small browser-control reference showing how to build and execute Jev action choices.
notes: A deliberately limited browser-control reference, not a general-purpose desktop driver. The source links a recorded walkthrough and explains the action loop. Inspect credential handling and permissions before installation; no live walkthrough was run here.

name: Jev Browser (MCP, CLI, library)
description: Playwright browser controlled by Jev, available as an MCP server, CLI, or library.
notes: Uses its own Playwright Chromium; installation may download a browser. Live actions need TypeSafe access, and text entry can use another provider. An early browser implementation, not a universal computer-use backend. Do not treat published demonstrations as independently reproduced.

name: Jev Browser Use (existing Codex connection)
description: Skill that uses an existing Codex browser connection. Jev clicks and scrolls; Codex types and checks the result.
notes: Reuses an existing browser connection; it does not install a new driver. The inspected README says browser execution currently requires Codex Computer Use; installability in another client does not prove execution support. Choose the skill or plugin to avoid duplicate instructions. Speed claims are workflow-specific author measurements.

name: Jevlike (independent option scorer)
description: Independent one-pass option scorer with training code and game examples. Not TypeSafe Jev.
notes: Not TypeSafe Jev weights or its unpublished architecture. Similar input/output shape does not establish equal quality. Selected game-video windows are not typical-play evidence; review checkpoint formats, model/data licenses, and evaluation controls before reuse.

name: CUA-S1-FORMS (independent specialist)
description: Cua's independent form-filling model and dataset. Not a general desktop agent or official Jev weights.
notes: Model and dataset Hub metadata were inspected; no weights were downloaded or inference run. The paired dataset is cua-ai/cua-s1-forms on Hugging Face. The GitHub component README describes a source-only research profile; do not equate that statement with absence of the separately published Hub artifact. Check exact artifact/model-card terms and task scope; no numerical performance claim is reproduced here.

name: llm-typesafe
description: Use Jev from the LLM command line or Python, with stdin, templates, and sync/async calls.
notes: Suggested by the author in issue #2. Reviewed the client and error tests, including redirect refusal and malformed JSON handling; no upstream tests or live inference were run here. Sends input to TypeSafe. The host LLM tool's normal logging can retain prompts and provider responses.

name: wellposed
description: Offline linter and agent skill for Jev requests: checks missing options, broken state references, and question types.
notes: Submitted in HN comment 49803528. Structural rules and tests were inspected, not executed. Structural lint is offline; --semantic makes paid TypeSafe calls and can send request state. Rules are heuristic and version-specific. The author's evaluation corpus is model-generated/labeled, so its reported scores are not independent validation.

name: nospace
description: Adds spaces while you type. Jev chooses between possible word splits; a separate model handles spelling corrections.
notes: Submitted in HN comment 49802812. Reviewed the provider code and tests for stale replies, caret preservation, undo, and composition input; no upstream tests or live model calls were run. English-only experimental demo; HN users reported ambiguous splits. Text reaches hosted inference through server routes, and spelling correction uses a separate paid model. Word list retains its MIT notice.

name: jevrs
description: Async Rust client with typed answers, derive macros, and native or WASI transports.
notes: Author submission in issue #4. Source review covered request framing, credential-redacted Debug, typed response/probability validation, retry tests, and native/WASI example source; no Rust build, WASI runtime, upstream test suite, or live API call was run. Unofficial client. Live inputs go to TypeSafe by default. Custom base URLs are caller-controlled and checked for URI syntax, not mandatory HTTPS: keep real credentials on trusted HTTPS endpoints. Configure transport timeouts and retry budgets. The X link was supplied by the author, not independently inspected in this pass.

name: jev-belay
description: Claude Code Stop hook that checks local run evidence before Jev judges an unverified completion claim.
notes: Submitted in PR #1. Local code establishes file-change/check evidence and fails open on errors; only redacted task/final-message text and derived counts are intended for inference. Author AUROC/latency/cost figures come from one author's model-labeled corpus and were not reproduced. Default inference is TypeSafe HTTPS; a custom JEV_BASE_URL is not forced to HTTPS, so use only trusted HTTPS endpoints with real credentials. Source-reviewed only; the hook and its upstream tests were not executed here.

name: jev-plays-pokemon-red
description: Pokemon Red agent where code builds legal actions and route state; Jev chooses only at branch points.
notes: Submitted in PR #1. Requires a lawful local Pokemon Red dump; the repository does not ship ROM or save-state game data. Unknown or failed model choices fall back to code-owned legal actions. Author timing/cost and cartridge behavior were not reproduced. Default inference is TypeSafe HTTPS; a custom JEV_BASE_URL should be a trusted HTTPS endpoint when a real bearer key is used. Source-reviewed only; no ROM, upstream tests, or live inference were run here.

name: jgrep (npm: jevgrep)
description: Jev answers one Noul per code chunk, diff hunk, or CSV row (does this match the description?); code prints the probabilities as file:line hits, gates CI on an English rule with --diff, and lists the test files a diff can affect with --tests.
notes: Every searched chunk is sent to TypeSafe; TypeSafe endpoint only. Maintainer submission.
